newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's bullish Morococha jumps on bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Peru's bullish Morococha jumps on bolsa.

text.p: For the second consecutive session, Morococha's share price jumped on the Lima Stock Exchange, rallying 7.84 percent in early trade Tuesday due to speculation the miner had found new reserves, brokers said.

Following its 10 percent rise Monday, Morococha stood at 6.05 soles in volume of 46,300 shares after one and a half hours' trade in the four hour session at 1030 local time (1530 GMT). The polymetallic miner's share has more than doubled its price since the beginning of May, when it stood at 2.77 soles.
Brokers explained that due to other circumstantial evidence, investors believed the market's rumors that the miner had found a new mineral resource.
The 27-percent stake buy in Morococha earlier this month by Phelps Dodge Corp "had to be for some particular reason," Augusto Larco of local brokerage Peruval said.

Normally when there is no formal announcement from a company that justifies such a bullish run in a stock -- as is the case currently of Morococha -- then the stock exchange suspends trade in the shares.
But players speculated that bolsa officials had contacted Morococha and received adequate justifications for the rises.
"There is definitely something behind (the rises) or the bolsa would have stopped trade," Larco said.
This month, Morococha -- along with another polymetallic miner Atacocha -- has led the sector's record bull run that has seen miners' liquid labor shares gain 125 percent since the start of the year.

The sector's rises -- evident mainly in zinc producers -- were due to elevated international zinc prices and solid company performances that were likely to yield healthy second quarter profits, brokers said.
